**Answer: Yes.**

**Proof.** Let $J \colon X \to X''$ denote the canonical isometric embedding, defined by $J(x)(f) = f(x)$ for $x \in X$, $f \in X'$. Recall that $J$ is a linear isometry: $\|J(x)\|_{X''} = \|x\|_X$ for every $x \in X$ (this is a consequence of the Hahn–Banach theorem).

Fix an arbitrary $x \in X$. Since $J(x) \in X''$, we may apply the hypothesis with $F = J(x)$. Observing that
$$J(x)(f_n) = f_n(x),$$
we obtain
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |f_n(x)| = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |J(x)(f_n)| \le C\,\|J(x)\|_{X''} = C\,\|x\|_X < \infty.$$

Since $x \in X$ was arbitrary, we conclude
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |f_n(x)| \le C\,\|x\| < \infty \quad \text{for all } x \in X.$$

In fact, the conclusion is stronger than what was asked: not only is the series finite for every $x$, but the map $x \mapsto (f_n(x))_{n\ge1}$ is a bounded linear operator $X \to \ell^1$ with operator norm at most $C$. The hypothesis is a statement about *all* of $X''$, and the canonical image $J(X) \subseteq X''$ is part of that domain, so the conclusion follows immediately by restriction. $\blacksquare$
